tagline: Out to the white dunes and back along the Henrys Fork.
intro: North of Rexburg the byway takes the Salem Highway out to the St. Anthony Sand Dunes, then the Red Road across BLM desert to County Road A-2, which crosses Camas Creek and runs north and east to Island Park. The Shoshone-Bannock came to the creek crossing to dig the bulbs of the camas lily.

A second leg follows the Henrys Fork, a fly-fishing river named for the trapper Andrew Henry. His post near St. Anthony, the first American fur post west of the Continental Divide, was abandoned the spring after it went up. From St. Anthony the old highway runs past Chester to Ashton.
season: Visit Idaho gives mid-April to mid-November as the time to go.

moments.title: St. Anthony Sand Dunes
moments.text: Wind has piled the sand of an Ice Age lakeshore into white quartz dunes up to 400 feet high, where some 2,500 elk winter and shed their antlers for spring collectors.

moments.title: Camas Meadows Battleground
moments.text: In 1877 Nez Perce warriors made off with the Army's pack animals here, and Captain Norwood's failed try to recover them left the soldiers unable to give chase.

moments.title: Ashton
moments.text: Ashton ran its first American Dog Derby in 1917, 55 miles down the unplowed rail line from West Yellowstone, and a blizzard kept the finish waiting two days.

practical: County Road A-2 is not plowed in winter and becomes a snowmobile trail.
